name: Waidring
kurzbeschreibung: Vacation village in the Pillerseetal valley with the Steinplatte ski area and breathtaking mountain views.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The traditional alpine municipality of Waidring is situated at an altitude of 778 metres above sea level in the Pillerseetal valley within the Kitzbühel district, nestled beneath the dramatic limestone ramparts of the Steinplatte (1,869 m) and the rugged Loferer Steinberge. Home to approximately 2,050 residents, this delightful village serves as the northern gateway to the Pillerseetal right at the tri-border point of Tyrol, Salzburg, and Bavaria. Sheltered between the Chiemgau and Kitzbühel Alps, Waidring presents itself as an all-season destination combining living Tyrolean heritage with modern leisure amenities. Renowned historically as the 'Bell Village' (Glockendorf) and famed for its prehistoric geological origins, Waidring draws families, alpine athletes, and nature seekers alike.

Geschichte

Archaeological investigations demonstrate that human presence in Waidring dates back to the early medieval era, with stone ecclesiastical foundations existing as early as 1200. The parish was officially documented in 1381. The community developed a distinctive historical identity through artisanal bell casting, gaining renown far beyond regional borders and earning the community its historic moniker as the 'Bell Village'. The late Baroque parish church dedicated to Saints Vitus and Nicholas was constructed between 1757 and 1764 under master builders Kassian Singer and Andreas Hueber. A remarkable interior detail is the church flooring fashioned from local stone quarried directly from the Steinplatte—a fossilised coral reef that formed more than 200 million years ago in the ancient Tethys Ocean.

Anreise

Waidring enjoys first-rate transport connections and is readily reachable from across Austria and neighbouring Germany. Motorists arriving from Germany can travel completely toll-free without an Austrian motorway vignette via the Inntal motorway A93/Kiefersfelden or via the Bavarian A8 motorway through Rosenheim and Kössen, following the Loferer federal road B178 straight into town. From Innsbruck or Salzburg, the B178 also offers convenient access. Rail travellers journey to nearby railway stations at St. Johann in Tirol or Fieberbrunn, where frequent regional buses of the Verkehrsverbund Tirol (routes 8302 and 4012) connect directly into the centre of Waidring.

Tipps

The premier summer attraction is Triassic Park on the Steinplatte mountain, an interactive prehistoric edutainment park featuring life-size dinosaurs, the Triassic Trail, a dramatic viewing platform suspended 70 metres over a sheer abyss, and a Triassic beach at 1,700 metres. Sport climbers prize the south-facing limestone walls of the Steinplatte as a world-class climbing destination. In winter, the cross-border Steinplatte-Winklmoosalm ski area offers 42 kilometres of snow-sure ski runs. Down in the valley, the Waidring bathing lake and leisure centre with its spring-fed lake, heated swimming pool, and sunbathing lawns provides refreshment, while the bell museum offers captivating insights into the ancient art of bell founding.
